text.p: Giant United States stock brokerage Merrill Lynch and Co Inc, which earlier on Tuesday announced an agreed A$117 million bid for local brokerage firm McIntosh Securities Ltd, said it had a confident outlook for markets in Australia and New Zealand.
"We are very positive about the outlook for this market and we expect to grow this business," executive vice president, corporate strategy and research, Jerome Kenney, told reporters.
"We are convinced that this will become a major market for us," Kenney said.

Merrill Lynch said in statements accompanying its takeover announcement that the purchase of McIntosh would give it a leading position in Australia and New Zealand equity and debt markets, as an underwriter and trader.
Kenney also said the New York-based broker is interested in moving into the funds management sector at some later stage but has not yet decided how this would be achieved.

McIntosh directors have recommended that shareholders accept the A$1.40 per share bid but have not received any view on the bid from 20 percent shareholder ING Bank of the Netherlands. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
